title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's integrated process for model onboarding into the Eval Harness, creation and curation of prompt sets and benchmarks, quantization profile selection, and regression triage workflows. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML Engineers, and Platform SREs who run model evaluation, ship model variants to serving, and manage quality guardrails.

Goals
- Standardize onboarding so new model variants enter the eval and serving lifecycle with repeatable checks.
- Provide a single source of truth for prompt sets, evaluation metrics, and quantization trade-offs.
- Ensure fast, deterministic regression triage and mitigation steps when a production regression is detected.

Scope
This document covers: eval-harness integration, prompt-set taxonomy and benchmark guidelines, model onboarding checklist and runbook, quality guardrails and alert thresholds, quantization profile evaluation, and regression triage playbook. It does not cover low-level kernel optimization decisions (see eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture) or commercial SLAs beyond the internal SLOs listed below.

Ownership and Roles
- Eval Harness Owner: Applied ML Team (primary contact: Aisha Patel).
- Model Onboarding Lead: Model Platform (Marcus Li).
- Quantization SME: Inference Research (Sofia Gomez).
- Incident/Regression Lead: Eng SRE on-call rotation.
- Consumer / Product QA: Customer-facing product team owning feature correctness.

High-level Process Flow
1) Model candidate submitted to eval-harness with metadata and artifact location.
2) Prompt set selection and automatic benchmark execution (functional + safety + perf).
3) Quantization profiles evaluated in sandbox (PTQ/QAT variants).
4) Results reviewed; quality guardrails validated.
5) If all checks pass, model is promoted to staging / canary serving with rollout policy.
6) If a regression is detected post-rollout, follow regression triage playbook.

Eval Harness (Service)
- Service name: eval-harness-service (internal).
- Core responsibilities: run prompt-set-driven evaluations, store results in eval-catalog, and emit alerts if guardrails are breached.
- API snippets: (example)
  POST /api/v1/eval/run
  {
    "model_version": "redwood-bert-xxl:2027-03-01",
    "prompt_sets": ["summarization-core-v2", "safety-blacklist-v1"],
    "profiles": ["fp16", "int8-ptq"]
  }

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Taxonomy:
  - Core functional sets: summarization-core, qa-core, codegen-core
  - Edge-case fuzz sets: hallucination-probes, factuality-stress
  - Safety & compliance: pii-detection, toxicity-checks, policy-coverage
- Creation guidelines:
  - Each prompt must include: intent label, input, expected-output or scoring rubric.
  - Minimum size: 100 examples for core functional sets; 500 for benchmark suites intended for model acceptance.
  - Benchmarks must have clear pass/fail thresholds and at least two automated scorers (e.g., exact-match + semantic similarity).

Recommended benchmark metrics (examples)
- Summarization: ROUGE-L (>= 0.48), SemanticSIM (> 0.72), hallucination-rate (< 4%).
- QA: Exact Match (>= 0.65), F1 (>= 0.78).
- Safety: toxicity-rate (< 0.2%), PII-detection recall (> 0.95).

Model Onboarding: Checklist and Runbook
Pre-submission checklist (required):
- Artifact present in model registry with versioned weights (S3 URI).
- Model card with architecture, training data summary, known limitations.
- Owner and emergency contact listed.
- Baseline performance on core prompt sets populated.

Onboarding runbook (numbered steps):
1. Submit a model bundle to eval-harness via the portal or CLI. Example CLI: evalctl submit --model s3://models/redwood-llm/v2 --meta meta.yaml
2. Select recommended prompt sets (system will suggest based on task classification).
3. Run default quantization profiles (see quantization section). Allow parallel jobs: perf + functional + safety.
4. Review automated report (eval-catalog URL returned by the service). Key artifacts: metric CSV, failure examples, scorer logs, latency distribution p95/p99.
5. Sign-off by Model Onboarding Lead and Applied ML owner before staging promotion.

Quality Guardrails and Alerting
- Guardrail categories: correctness, safety, latency, cost (tokens/sec economics).
- Example guardrails and thresholds (applied as automated checks pre-promotion and as runtime monitors):
  - Functional regression: >5% relative drop in semantic similarity vs baseline triggers auto-block.
  - Safety failure: any increase in PII-detection false negatives beyond 1% absolute triggers incident.
  - Latency: p99 > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes continuous -> page SRE.
  - Cost delta: >20% token cost increase without quality improvement -> notify infra & product.
- Alerting channels: PagerDuty (critical), #applied-ml-evals Slack (high), email summary to reviewers (medium).

Quantization Profiles and Evaluation
- Profiles maintained in repo: infra/quantization-profiles. Each profile is named and includes expected accuracy trade-offs and recommended hardware.
- Example profiles (table):
  | profile-name | method | expected-accuracy-delta | recommended-hardware | notes |
  | fp16 | FP16 baseline | 0% | A100/V100 | default training/serving profile |
  | int8-ptq | PTQ linear-only | 1-3% drop | T4/A10 | fast, low-compute option |
  | int8-qat | QAT | 0-1% drop | A100 | best accuracy but longer workflow |

Quantization evaluation steps:
1. Run functional + perf evals on quantized artifact in sandbox serving.
2. Compare metrics vs fp16 baseline; generate delta report.
3. If accuracy drop exceeds profile target, mark profile as failed for this model and include failure examples for triage.

Regression Triage Playbook (post-release)
Purpose: rapidly identify root cause and rollback or mitigate when production regressions are detected.
Severity definitions:
- Sev1 (Critical): user-facing correctness loss impacting >1% of requests or safety breaches. PagerDuty page and immediate rollback.
- Sev2 (High): performance degradation (latency/cost) or correctness loss localized to a feature; Slack escalation.

Triage steps (numbered):
1. Acknowledge alert and create incident ticket (incident template: Applied-ML Regression).
2. Gather artifacts: recent eval-harness report for deployed model, serving logs (p95/p99, error rates), sampled requests and responses, prompt set hits.
3. Quick checks: compare to last known-good eval-catalog snapshot (tools: evalctl diff --baseline <id> --candidate <id>).
4. If clear model regression, initiate immediate mitigation: either rollback to last-known-good or enable automatic fallback routing to a safer model variant.
5. If not obvious, create a reproducible test case and run targeted prompt sets in eval-harness (mark as high-priority).
6. Postmortem: owner documents root cause, impact, and corrective actions within 72 hours. Required fields: timeline, root cause, remediation plan, tester sign-off.

Mitigation templates
- Rollback: set rollout_policy = "rollback" in serving-config; activate emergency flag.
- Canary shrink: reduce new model traffic to 0% and increase baseline model to 100% for 15 minutes before re-evaluation.

Operational tooling and commands
- evalctl list-prompt-sets
- evalctl submit --model <s3-uri> --prompt-sets summarization-core,hallucination-probes --profiles fp16,int8-ptq
- evalctl status --run <run-id>
- evalctl diff --baseline <id> --candidate <id> --metrics semantic-similarity,rouge-l

Reporting and Documentation
- Every onboarding produces an eval-catalog entry with: run-id, model-version, prompt-sets, metric csv links, failure-examples (min 20), quantization-deltas, and owner sign-off.
- Monthly digest: Applied ML team publishes a monthly regression digest summarizing incidents, root causes, and trends.

Appendix: Example eval report snippet (CSV header)
- run_id,model_version,prompt_set,metric_name,metric_value,baseline_value,delta
- 20270301-42,redwood-llm-v2,summarization-core,semantic_similarity,0.751,0.768,-0.017
